questions.text: What is the largest organ of the human body?
questions.hostNotes: Not the liver, which is the largest internal organ.

questions.text: How many chambers does the human heart have?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: 4. Two atria and two ventricles.

questions.text: Which vitamin does your skin make when exposed to sunlight?
What mosquito-borne disease, common in the Philippine rainy season, can cause a dangerous drop in platelets?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: dengue fever. Spread by Aedes mosquitoes.

questions.text: What is the normal human body temperature in degrees Celsius, to the nearest degree?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: 37, 36 to 37.

questions.text: Which pair of bean-shaped organs filter the blood and make urine?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: kidney, bato.

questions.text: Which type of blood cell fights infection?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: leukocytes, WBC.

questions.text: What deadly viral disease can people get from the bite of an infected dog?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: rabis.

questions.text: What is the medical term for high blood pressure?
questions.hostNotes: Not hypotension, which is low blood pressure.

questions.text: What is the traditional Filipino healing massage called?
questions.hostNotes: A practitioner is called a manghihilot.

questions.text: Which organs does tuberculosis mainly attack?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: baga.

questions.text: How many bones does an adult human have?
Including wisdom teeth, how many teeth does a full adult set have?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: thirty-two.

questions.text: What is the colored part of the eye called?
questions.hostNotes: Not the pupil, which is the black opening in its center.

questions.text: What is the longest bone in the human body?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: thigh bone.

questions.text: What is the largest internal organ of the human body?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: atay.

questions.text: Which organ produces insulin?
What iron-rich protein in red blood cells carries oxygen?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: haemoglobin.

questions.text: A lack of which vitamin causes scurvy?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: ascorbic acid.

questions.text: Which butterfly-shaped gland in the neck controls the body's metabolism?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: thyroid gland.

questions.text: What tube carries food from the mouth to the stomach?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: oesophagus, gullet. Not the trachea, which carries air.

questions.text: What disease can people catch by wading through floodwater contaminated with rat urine?
What herbal plant, approved by the Department of Health, is a common Filipino remedy for cough?
questions.hostNotes: Not sambong, which is used for kidney stones and as a diuretic. Yerba buena is also DOH-approved, mainly for pain; accept it at the host's discretion.

questions.text: Which Filipino hero trained as an eye doctor and operated on his own mother's eyes?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Rizal, Jose Rizal. He trained in ophthalmology in Europe.

questions.text: What is the common name for the clavicle?
What is the common name for the tympanic membrane?
What is the yellowish liquid part of blood called?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: blood plasma. Not serum, which is plasma without clotting factors.

questions.text: "Bulutong-tubig" is the Filipino name for what itchy, blistery childhood disease?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: varicella. Not measles, which is tigdas.

questions.text: Which small organ under the liver stores bile?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: apdo.

questions.text: Which blood type is known as the universal donor?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: O-. Not plain type O: O positive gives only to positive types. AB positive is the universal recipient.

questions.text: Which ancient Greek physician is called the "Father of Medicine"?
questions.hostNotes: The Hippocratic Oath is named after him.

questions.text: What does CPR stand for?
What is the medical name for the kneecap?
What is the medical name for the tailbone?
What organ, also called the voice box, holds the vocal cords?
questions.hostNotes: Not the pharynx (throat) or trachea (windpipe).

questions.text: Which part of the brain controls balance and coordination?
questions.hostNotes: Not the cerebrum.

questions.text: What are the tiny air sacs in the lungs where oxygen enters the blood called?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: alveolus.

questions.text: What is the smallest bone in the human body?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: stirrup. It is in the middle ear.

questions.text: What is the longest nerve in the human body, running from the lower back down each leg?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: sciatic.

questions.text: What "feel-good" chemicals does the brain release during exercise to relieve pain?
Which hormone, made when it gets dark, helps regulate sleep?
A lack of vitamin B1, or thiamine, causes what disease?
What Filipino word refers to a relapse after an illness or childbirth, blamed on overexertion?
Which English doctor developed the first vaccine, against smallpox, in 1796?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Jenner. He used material from cowpox sores.

questions.text: Which American scientist developed the first widely used polio vaccine in the 1950s?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Salk. Albert Sabin later developed the oral polio vaccine.
